receipts.first_text_witness: I want to tell you about two brothers, Carter and Colton. Same parents, same house, same Cincinnati suburb, same underfunded public school. Their dad drove a city bus for 32 years. When they both graduated and started working, they each took home roughly $3,200 a month after taxes. Fast forward to today, Carter is 46. He books last minute flights on a Tuesday because he felt like seeing a friend in Austin. He doesn't check his account first, he just books it. Colton is 44. He makes $95,000 a year, about twice what Carter makes. On Sunday nights, he opens his banking app and does the math one more time quietly while his wife is already asleep, hoping the number changed since Thursday.
receipts.last_text_witness: money arrives in an ordinary week that nobody around you will ever notice, but you will in 20 years on a Tuesday when you book a flight without checking your account first. If this one hit different, subscribe. We cover this every week. Drop a comment below. Which generation do you think got hit hardest by this trap and why? I'll be reading everyone. See you in the next video.
